task: Inspect a JavaScript or Electron application without executing it

x-display.title: See how a JavaScript app fits together
x-display.summary: Map an app’s modules, imports and Electron boundaries, with evidence you can inspect later.
x-display.description:
Give your agent an extracted JavaScript application or an ASAR archive. REA analyses the files locally and saves its findings, their evidence and the limits of the analysis. Your agent can then investigate the saved result without repeatedly analysing the app.

This setup supplies REA’s static JavaScript workflow and command line. It does not install a desktop disassembler, execute the application or establish what its code does at runtime. For native binary analysis, follow REA’s own provider setup.

packaging_note: Uses the checksummed official rea-agents 6.8.0 npm archive and its published runtime. Its npm provenance names the pinned source commit. Includes procps for upstream's Linux process checks.

inputs.what: an extracted JavaScript/Electron application folder, or an ASAR archive; the helper stages either at this path

outputs.what: REA's complete static analysis, including evidence and limitations
a compact view of the saved evidence

commands.name: rea
commands.what: REA's provider-free inspection commands, including views of saved evidence

settings.name: REA_TIMEOUT
settings.what: maximum analysis time in seconds; defaults to 600
settings.how: Choose 10–1800. Large applications may need more time and memory; a timed-out analysis is a failure, not a partial success.

known_issues: Static analysis can be incomplete for obfuscated code, dynamic imports and missing files. Read the result's coverage and limitations. This CPU setup has a 4 GB memory limit.

Keep the full app directory, including manifests and source maps. A single JavaScript file is not the application-directory workflow. Network access and host GUI/native-analysis providers are not included.
licence: REA MIT; bundled third-party notices are retained in its npm package. UGT's driver and checks are Apache-2.0.
